NRL Late Mail: Round 25 - Latrell on hold; Turbo on track
Superstar Latrell Mitchell will target a return in Round 26 against the Titans after his long-awaited comeback was put on hold.
Mitchell has missed 11 games as he battles nerve pain in his lower back which has affected his leg and calf but had been named in the Rabbitohs' extended squad on Tuesday.
"There was a chance (for this week). He trained pretty well but just probably needs another week," coach Wayne Bennett said on Friday.
"We took a cautious approach and we'll give him another week."
Better news for Manly though with Tom Trbojevic a confirmed starter for their clash with the Knights on Saturday.

The Bulldogs will put their finals hopes on the line when they take on the resurgent Dragons at Allianz Stadium.
Plenty has changed since the two teams opened the season in Las Vegas, with Canterbury skipper Stephen Crichton kicking a golden point field goal to deliver his side a memorable victory.

Cameron Ciraldo's side must now win at least two of their final three games and hope other results go their way to play finals football.
Standing in their way this week is a Dragons side that has claimed back-to-back victories and is desperate to avoid the wooden spoon.
St George Illawarra held on to edge the Tigers last weekend, with a promising crop of young forwards getting better with each week.
Hamish Stewart has rocketed into Australian World Cup contention, while prop Loko Pasifiki Tonga is sending a message up front.

NRL Casualty Ward: Surgery for Doueihi, Walsh; Turbo good to go
Wests Tigers halfback Adam Doueihi will undergo season-ending surgery that will rule him out of Lebanon's World Cup campaign.
The playmaker dislocated his shoulder in a Round 9 loss to the Sharks and initially delayed surgery in an attempt to kickstart the Tigers finals campaign.
The 28-year-old returned to the field in Round 17 but fresh scans have shown Doueihi requires immediate surgery, with the halfback to go under the knife later this week.
"New scans on Adam's shoulder have showed the time has come to have his reconstruction done. This gives him enough time to be ready for the start of the 2027 season," Wests Tigers head of high performance Peter Moussa said.
Meanwhile, Tigers five-eighth Latu Fainu has suffered a low-grade hamstring injury at training. Fainu was set to return this week after serving a three-game suspension but will now be sidelined for 1-2 weeks with his latest injury.
In positive news, Sunia Turuva has been named on the six-man bench despite suffering a knee injury last week, while Alex Twal is set to return after missing Round 24 due to illness.
Broncos superstar Reece Walsh has had surgery on his ankle and is facing an eight-week recovery time.
Walsh had scans on Sunday which confirmed he had sustained a high-grade syndesmosis injury during the loss to the Warriors on Saturday night.
Warriors fullback Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad has subsequently been banned for two games for a hip drop tackle.
With Australia's World Cup opener against the Kiwis set down for Thursday, October 15 it appears Walsh's chances of representing the Kangaroos are gone.
The Raiders had Simi Sasagi back from a shoulder injury for their clash with the Broncos but lost back-rower Zac Hosking to a hamstring injury during the second half.
South Sydney star Latrell Mitchell will look to return in Round 26 from a nerve injury that has kept him sidelined since Round 11.
The centre has missed 11 games with the injury but was named in the Bunnies' extended squad for this weekend's match against the Warriors before being put on ice once more.
The Rabbitohs have lost Adam Elliott to a groin injury, with the veteran expected to miss two to three weeks with a strained adductor.
Meanwhile, Warriors halfback Luke Metcalf will miss the remainder of the regular season after suffering a hamstring injury in last week's win over Brisbane.
"The timeline for him will be deep into the finals but you never know," coach Andrew Webster said on Thursday.
"I think this is probably the most optimistic I've seen him when he knows he's got a plan and when he knows he wants to attack something."

A win but still stuck at the bottom
On the road against the Tigers, the Dragons held on for a narrow 24-22 victory which was spirited and provides hope moving forward. As ugly as it was, they will take the 2-competition points. With just 47% possession they completed at 82% which gave them the ability to run for 9.5m per carry and create 5 line breaks. It demonstrated their attacking ability; they still have their shortcomings in defence though. Missing 30 tackles, better teams will make them pay for their mistakes in the future. Perhaps this demonstrates their immaturity, and it will give them an area to focus on in the closing weeks of 2026.
Hanging on by a thread

With their fate in their hands, the Bulldogs were disappointing. They were outplayed in every way. With just 45% possession, they completed at 77% and made just 7.7m per carry. This saw them also create just 1 line break and miss 41 tackles. Given such a performance with everything to play for, doubt remains whether they deserve the opportunity to progress beyond the regular season.

The Rabbitohs sit seventh and are trying to lock away their finals position, while New Zealand remain third and level on competition points with Penrith as they chase a top 2 finish and a home final.
Both teams therefore have plenty to play for, but I still lean toward the Warriors despite the disruption in their spine. Luke Metcalf is sidelined with a hamstring injury, Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad is suspended, and Andrew Webster has named Chanel Harris-Tavita at halfback alongside rookie Luke Hanson, who plays just his second NRL game. Rabbitohs Building Momentum at the Right Time
South Sydney continued their late season surge with a convincing 22-6 victory over Canterbury last Friday, another crucial step toward securing a finals berth after a season that has contained more than its fair share of disruption. Matt Dufty has been one of the success stories of South Sydney’s resurgence. Against Canterbury he produced 250 running metres, four tackle breaks, a try and a try assist, giving the Rabbitohs the type of support play and yardage they desperately needed during their injury riddled middle of the season.
The bigger improvement has come through the return of their forward leaders. Cameron Murray and David Fifita have both made an immediate impact since returning, and South Sydney look far more capable of sustaining pressure through the middle rather than asking Cody Walker to manufacture everything himself. Friday Night Football at GIO Stadium has far more riding on it than the respective ladder positions suggest, as the Raiders host Brisbane in a matchup loaded with desperation, emotion, and a little revenge. Canberra’s finals hopes remain incredibly faint, but they are still alive. Wins over Brisbane and North Queensland, combined with their Round 26 bye, could get the Raiders to 30 competition points, and leave them praying other results fall their way. Brisbane, meanwhile, have endured one of the worst premiership defences in modern NRL history and are now fighting simply to avoid an unthinkable wooden spoon.
Then there is Josh Papali’i. Friday night will be the Canberra legend’s final home appearance, with GIO Stadium even being temporarily transformed into “Papa’s House” for the occasion. Papali’i has been promoted into the starting front row, and you can guarantee the Raiders faithful will turn this into one of the most emotional home games of the season.

Canberra looked like a team whose finals hopes were virtually finished heading into last week’s trip to Sharks Stadium, yet they produced one of their gutsiest performances of the season to upset Cronulla 24-20. Against a Sharks side sitting firmly in the top 4 conversation, the Raiders absorbed an early 8-0 deficit, fought their way to an 18-14 halftime lead and then survived a frantic final quarter to keep their season alive.
Joseph Tapine delivered the decisive moment after the Sharks had regained a 20-18 advantage, powering through five defenders to score underneath the posts in the 57th minute. From there, Canberra defended their lead despite Cronulla receiving several opportunities to steal the game late.
It was exactly the type of performance Ricky Stuart would have wanted after the Raiders’ form had again become inconsistent. Canberra have enough attacking talent through Kaeo Weekes, Ethan Strange, Ethan Sanders, Matthew Timoko and Xavier Savage, but their success still starts with the middle. There are three rounds remaining in the 2026 NRL regular season and wobbling heavyweights Penrith and Cronulla will be desperate to recover from back-to-back losses this weekend against out-of-contention opposition.
Manly and Canterbury face must-win assignments, while South Sydney has a huge obstacle in front of them in the form of the Warriors.
Read on for our complete 2026 NRL Round 25 predictions, tips and best Rugby League bets to place this weekend!
The finals ship has all but sailed for Melbourne, but knocking over stumbling Penrith in their last home game of the season will provide ample motivation.
FORM: The Storm snapped a three-game losing run to trounce the Sea Eagles 42-20 in Perth in Round 23, after trailing at halftime. They had the bye last weekend.
The Panthers lost their grip on top spot courtesy of a 12-6 loss to the Roosters – their fifth loss in eight games.
INS AND OUTS: Melbourne gets a further boost with Harry Grant and Jack Howarth returning, which sees Tyran Wishart and Joe Chan revert to the bench. Trent Toelau will partner Cam Munster in the halves this week.
Casey McLean is a back in a timely lift for the Panthers, with Paul Alamoti (hamstring) ruled out.
KEY MATCH-UP: Different jersey numbers, but Origin adversaries and Test teammates Munster and Nathan Cleary will guide their teams’ fortunes.
HISTORY: The Storm have won four of their last six against the Panthers but crashed to a 50-10 loss at CommBank Stadium in Round 5.
KEY STAT: The Panthers have a 1-9 record at AAMI Park.
VERDICT: The two biggest heavyweights of the 2020s renew a fierce rivalry, though at a very different juncture than the out-of-contention Storm are used to. But the injury-ravaged side has been gallant in recent defeats and the win over Manly was well-deserved reward.
There’s plenty at stake for the Panthers, who could drop out of the top two with a loss and need to recover some momentum over the closing three rounds.
The Storm are a tempting option with a 7.5-point start after winning five of their last six at home, but the over appeals more with seven of 10 games at AAMI Park producing 52-plus points this season.
Predictions: Back Over 42.5 Total Points @ $1.90
SGM: STORM +7.5 / OVER 7.5 TOTAL TRIES / TOM JENKINS ANYTIME TRYSCORER / NICK MEANEY ANYTIME TRYSCORER @ $16.31
Other teams’ stumbles have maintained a mathematical Top 8 chance for the Raiders after an upset victory last week, but the spiralling Broncos’ only remaining motivation is avoiding the wooden spoon.
FORM: The Raiders showed an abundance of spirit to roll Cronulla 24-20 on the road last Saturday just six days after a seemingly season-ending home loss to Newcastle.
The Broncos crashed to their 12th loss in 13 games last weekend, a 40-6 defeat to the Warriors in which enthusiasm and defensive desire appeared sorely lacking – as well as costing them Reece Walsh for the rest of a sorry title defence.
INS AND OUTS: The Raiders get Simi Sasagi back from injury, Ata Mariota comes in at lock for Morgan Smithies (concussion) and Josh Papalii will start at prop in his last home game. Corey Horsburgh has received a bench recall.
Hayze Perham slots in as Brisbane’s fullback for Walsh, while Ben Hunt replaces Tom Duffy at halfback.
KEY MATCH-UP: Big ‘Papa’ will be fired up to turn back the clock in his home farewell – and he and Joe Tapine will engage in a crucial battle up front against Broncos bookends Xavier Willison and Payne Haas.
HISTORY: The Broncos have won three of their last four against the Raiders, most recently taking out a golden point epic at GIO Stadium 29-28 last September.
KEY STAT: Broncos wingers have scored 14 tries in the club’s last seven clashes with the Raiders. Both wingers scored in four of those matches.
VERDICT: A heavy loss to Penrith in Mudgee aside, the Raiders have been very competitive over the past seven weeks – winning five games – and will still be alive in the finals race when this game kicks off.
